name: Rufus
overview: Rufus is a male figure mentioned in the New Testament, specifically identified as the son of Simon the Cyrene. Beyond this unique attribute, Scripture does not provide further details about his tribe or additional notes. His mention is brief but distinct in the biblical record.
namesAndTitles: The name Rufus appears as a proper name in the Scriptures without any specific meaning or divine origin noted. It is simply recorded as Rufus in Mark 15:21, with no additional titles or meanings provided.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Rufus as the son of Simon the Cyrene. No other family relationships are documented beyond this connection, and no further relatives are mentioned in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Rufus holds significance primarily through his identification as the son of Simon the Cyrene, who is known for carrying the cross of Jesus. This connection places Rufus within the context of the Passion narrative, highlighting a family linked to the events surrounding Christ's crucifixion. Although Rufus himself is not the focus of extensive narrative, his mention underscores the personal and familial dimensions present in the Gospel accounts.
